question: Does a second win-probability model, with a stronger pregame layer from rolling-origin Projected Impact ratings, an overtime specialist and two more training seasons, give lower log loss than the frozen served model (courtlens-win-probability-v2, frozen 2026-11-04) on the same 2024-25 and 2025-26 states, and then on the same 2026-27 games after its own freeze?
inputs: Everything courtlens-win-probability-v2 reads, unchanged: its game table and state files under data/derived/win-probability-v1 (same content hashes), boxes, rating snapshots and benchmarks
The frozen served model's saved probabilities for every 2024-25 and 2025-26 state (data/derived/win-probability-v1/predictions/selected), the reference for gate A1

Projected Impact inputs as registered in courtlens-projected-impact-v1 (season features up to each opener, one-season RAPM targets 2016-17 to 2025-26), refitted per origin season with that registration's selected LightGBM settings
Benchmarks only, never inputs: ESPN per-play win probability (test seasons) and the hoopR-nba-data closing spread at commit 7be25dae, as in v2
method: v2 stays as it is: its files, version and live scorecard are untouched. v3 is a separate model with its own artifacts, freeze and scorecard.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-11: the betting line is a benchmark only, never an input; the gates read the same test games as v2 (a second read of those seasons, labelled as such), and the verdict is the head-to-head on 2026-27 games after v3's freeze.
States, views, weights, targets, metrics, the overtime tie rule and the Brownian baseline are v2's rules unchanged. v2's step S3, S4 and S5 inputs are not used: they were rejected in v2.

B (base): v2's selected recipe refitted on v3's splits. Team-form half-life chosen on train seasons from v2's grid; mu0 = v2's OLS columns fitted on 2015-16 to 2022-23; baseline beta and sigma and the overtime slope on train seasons; boosters with v2's base, S1 and S2 inputs, v2's selected num_leaves and every other v2 booster setting; the end-game specialist exactly as v2 (states with 120 seconds or less in period 4 or later, linear blend).

P1 (Projected Impact strength): for each target season t from 2018-19, a Projected Impact projection for every player in t's population from LightGBM with courtlens-projected-impact-v1's selected settings (4 leaves, min_data_in_leaf 20, 150 rounds, seed 2501), trained only on targets 2016-17 to t-1; rookies and returners take those training seasons' group means, and a player with no row takes the rookie mean. For 2026-27 the fit uses 2016-17 to 2025-26 and is frozen with v3. Team PI strength = sum over v2's stored roster of (expected-minutes share / 48) x projection. mu0_P1 = OLS of final margin on v2's columns plus PI strength difference x expected pace / 100, fitted on 2018-19 to 2022-23; games before 2018-19 keep B's mu0. P1 also adds the PI strength difference to the booster inputs.

P3 (overtime specialist): the end-game specialist is also fitted on and applied to every overtime state, with blend weight 1 throughout overtime; regulation keeps v2's linear blend over the last 120 seconds.

Selection on 2023-24 only, in order P1 then P3, each against the current accepted model: accepted when the paired game-bootstrap 90% interval of its log-loss improvement is above zero (P1 on all states, P3 on overtime states). A rejected step does not block the next.

P4 (final fit): the accepted recipe refitted on 2014-15 to 2023-24 (pregame OLS on 2015-16 to 2023-24, P1's OLS on 2018-19 to 2023-24), each booster and the specialist with the number of rounds early stopping chose on 2023-24. This final fit is the candidate v3; it is not selected, it is the registered procedure.
Test: read 2024-25 and 2025-26 once, after P4 is frozen. The reference is the frozen served model's saved probability for each state.
selection: On 2023-24 only: P1, then P3, each accepted when the paired game-bootstrap 90% interval (2000 replicates) of its log-loss improvement over the current accepted model is above zero; P1 on all states, P3 on overtime states. B is the starting model. P4 is not a selection step. The test seasons are read once, after P4 is fitted and frozen.
uncertainty: Game bootstrap, 2000 replicates, seed 2501, for every metric and paired difference, overall and by v2's phases. Prospective head-to-head: the same paired game bootstrap on 2026-27 games.
evaluation: Pooled and per-season log loss, Brier score and calibration curves for v3, B and the frozen served model on 2024-25 and 2025-26, overall and by phase
Paired differences, with 95% intervals: v3 against the frozen served model (gate A1), B against the frozen served model (what the refit alone does), v3 against B
Every selection result on 2023-24, accepted or not
ESPN comparison on matched states as in v2, for v3 and the frozen model side by side
Pregame margin RMSE and winner accuracy for v3's mu0, v2's mu0 and the closing spread on the same test games

Prospective: v3 against the frozen served model on the same 2026-27 games tipping after v3's freeze, with a 95% paired interval, reported from 25 games; until 300 games the page says it is too early to call
acceptance: A1: pooled test log loss of v3 beats the frozen served model on the same states, with the paired 95% game-bootstrap interval of the improvement above zero
A2: pooled test expected calibration error (20 equal-width bins) is 0.02 or less
Freeze checks, after A1 and A2: states built from ESPN change v3's test log loss by no more than 0.002, and p95 scoring time is 100 ms or less per full game on one thread
If A1 or A2 fails, v3 is not frozen or served, and the result is published on the page and in the evidence. The prospective head-to-head is reported, never a gate.
outputs: Artifacts under data/derived/win-probability-v3 (pregame, ladder, models, predictions, test report)
If frozen: evaluation/research/frozen/courtlens-win-probability-v3.json and hashed model files in the artifact registry, served beside v2
docs/evidence/finish/f05: report with every metric, the selection log, comparisons and runtimes
limitations: The test seasons are a second read: v2's test results on these seasons shaped v3's design (P1 targets the pregame gap, P3 the overtime calibration). Only the 2026-27 head-to-head after v3's freeze is a fully fresh test.
About 14,000 game outcomes, so the effective sample is games, not states
Projected Impact exists only from 2018-19 (it needs two earlier target seasons), so training seasons 2014-15 to 2017-18 keep B's mu0
Overtime is rare (about 60 games a season), so P3's selection has little power
Selection and early stopping share 2023-24, so selection-season improvements are optimistic
Live uses ESPN's roster minus reported Out at tip-off, as v2 does; the test assumes the inactive list is known
negative_result_policy: Publish every result, including failed gates, rejected steps and any loss to the frozen model, ESPN or the market, in the evidence and on the page. A failed gate is not re-run with changed settings under this identity; a change needs a new version.
